correctness.rationale: The shortest roots impose |x_i|+|x_j|<=1. In a sorted positive chamber those inequalities reduce to x_1+x_2<=1, and each of the five simplex vertices is a convex combination of the unit axial/half-coordinate vectors. Thus this polytope has radius at most one and the remaining lattice bisectors (vectors of length at least two) are redundant; the displayed unit vertices attain radius one. Independently integrated even monomials without the sorted-simplex coordinates: one positive orthant is the half-unit four-cube and four disjoint caps, one for each coordinate x_i>1/2 in which the remaining coordinates range independently from 0 to 1-x_i. Integrating each cap by a binomial expansion and applying orthant symmetry gives volume two and the normalized moments 13/120, 3/112, 1/112, 251/26880, 403/241920, 5/6912 for exponent patterns 2, 4, 22, 6, 42, 222. Odd-coordinate terms vanish. The Hadamard symmetry also verifies A_4=3B_4, so the fourth directional polynomial is radial with coefficient 3/112. Multinomial coefficients 1,15,90 give the full sixth polynomial. The axial gap is (3A_6-15B_6)/4=61/80640. The same independent integral verifies the radial moments, squared-radius variance and standardized fourth moment under the stated normalization.
